questions.text: Calculate the number of electrons constituting one coulomb of charge.
hints: Recall the quantization formula Q = n * e.
The elementary charge of an electron is e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C.

questions.text: A current of 0.5 A is drawn by a filament of an electric bulb for 10 minutes. Find the amount of electric charge that flows through the circuit.
questions.explanation: Given I = 0.5 A, time t = 10 minutes = 10 * 60 = 600 s. Q = I * t = 0.5 * 600 = 300 C.
hints: Time must be converted from minutes to SI unit seconds.
Use formula Q = I * t.

questions.text: Two identical bulbs are connected in series with a 6V battery. Bulb 1 is placed closer to the positive terminal, and Bulb 2 is placed closer to the negative terminal. Which bulb is brighter?

options.A: Bulb 1 is brighter because current enters it first
options.B: Both bulbs glow with equal brightness
options.C: Bulb 2 is brighter because negative electrons enter it first
options.D: Neither bulb glows because current cannot reach the second bulb

questions.explanation: Current is identical at every point in a series circuit. Electric charge is not consumed by the bulbs. Since identical bulbs carry the same current, they glow with equal brightness.
hints: Consider what electric current represents and whether charge is conserved.
Does current decrease as it passes through a series resistor?

questions.text: How should an ammeter be connected in an electric circuit to measure current flowing through a resistor?

options.A: Always in parallel across the resistor
options.B: Always in series with the resistor
options.C: Either in series or parallel, it gives the same reading
options.D: Across the terminals of the battery only

questions.explanation: An ammeter has very low resistance and must be connected in series so all the circuit current flows through it without altering the total resistance.
hints: Think about what happens to current in series vs parallel branches.
An ideal ammeter has zero internal resistance.

questions.text: How much work is done in moving a charge of 2 C across two points having a potential difference 12 V?
hints: Recall definition of potential difference: V = W / Q.
Rearrange to solve for work W.

questions.text: A switch in a series circuit with a battery and light bulb is moved from before the bulb to after the bulb. When the switch is opened, what happens?

options.A: The bulb stays on because current reaches it before the open switch
options.B: The bulb turns off immediately because the circuit loop is broken
options.C: The bulb flickers because current partially returns to the battery
options.D: The battery explodes due to charge accumulation

questions.explanation: An open switch interrupts the entire conductive path. For electric current to flow, there must be a complete closed loop. Its position in a single series loop does not matter.
hints: Think about the definition of a closed electric circuit.
Can current flow if any part of a series loop is disconnected?

questions.text: The potential difference across the terminals of an electric heater is 60 V when it draws a current of 4 A from the source. What current will the heater draw if the potential difference is increased to 120 V?
questions.explanation: Resistance R = V / I = 60 / 4 = 15 Ω. When V' = 120 V, new current I' = V' / R = 120 / 15 = 8 A.
hints: Find the resistance of the heater element first using Ohm's Law.
Use the calculated resistance to find current at 120 V.

questions.text: A cylindrical wire of copper is stretched so that its length increases by a factor of 2 while its volume remains constant. What happens to its resistance and resistivity?
questions.explanation: When length doubles (L' = 2L) and volume is constant (A*L = constant), area halves (A' = A/2). New resistance R' = ρ*(2L)/(A/2) = 4 * ρ(L/A) = 4R. Resistivity ρ is an intrinsic property of copper and does NOT change.
hints: Volume of a wire is Volume = Area * Length.
What is the difference between resistance (a property of geometry) and resistivity (a material property)?

questions.text: Three resistors of 5 Ω, 10 Ω, and 30 Ω are connected in series to a 12 V battery. What is the total equivalent resistance and the current through the 10 Ω resistor?
questions.explanation: For series resistors, R_s = 5 + 10 + 30 = 45 Ω. Current I = V / R_s = 12 / 45 = 0.267 A ≈ 0.27 A. The same current flows through all components.
hints: Series resistance is R_s = R1 + R2 + R3.
In a series circuit, current through each component is identical.

questions.text: Two resistors of 10 Ω and 40 Ω are connected in parallel across a 20 V battery. What is the equivalent resistance of the combination?
questions.explanation: 1/R_p = 1/10 + 1/40 = 4/40 + 1/40 = 5/40 = 1/8. Thus R_p = 8 Ω. Notice that equivalent resistance is smaller than the smallest branch resistor (10 Ω).
hints: Use reciprocal formula: 1/R_p = 1/R1 + 1/R2.
Don't forget to take the reciprocal after summing fractions!

questions.text: A 12 V battery is connected across two parallel branches: Branch A has resistance 3 Ω, and Branch B has resistance 6 Ω. How does the total current split?

options.A: Current splits equally: 3 A through each branch
options.B: 4 A flows through Branch A (3 Ω) and 2 A flows through Branch B (6 Ω)
options.C: 2 A flows through Branch A (3 Ω) and 4 A flows through Branch B (6 Ω)
options.D: All 6 A flows through Branch A because it has lower resistance

questions.explanation: Potential difference is 12 V across both branches. I_A = 12 / 3 = 4 A. I_B = 12 / 6 = 2 A. Lower resistance branch takes higher current.
hints: Calculate current in each branch independently using I = V / R.
Does current divide 50/50 when resistances are different?

questions.text: 100 J of heat is produced each second in a 4 Ω resistance. Find the potential difference across the resistor.
questions.explanation: Rate of heat production H/t = P = 100 W. P = V^2 / R => 100 = V^2 / 4 => V^2 = 400 => V = 20 V.
hints: Heat produced per second is electric power: H/t = P.
Recall the formula relating power, voltage, and resistance: P = V^2 / R.

questions.text: Two electric bulbs rated (40 W, 220 V) and (100 W, 220 V) are connected in series across a 220 V supply. Which bulb will glow brighter?

options.A: The 100 W bulb because it has a higher wattage rating
options.B: The 40 W bulb because its resistance is higher and series current is the same
options.C: Both bulbs will glow with their rated brightness
options.D: Neither bulb will glow because voltage is insufficient

questions.explanation: Bulb resistance is R = V^2 / P. Thus R_40 = 220^2 / 40 = 1210 Ω, while R_100 = 220^2 / 100 = 484 Ω. In series, both bulbs carry the same current I. Power dissipated is P_actual = I^2 * R. Because R_40 > R_100, the 40 W bulb dissipates more power and glows brighter!
hints: Find the resistance of each bulb from its rating using R = V^2 / P.
In a series circuit, current is common: compare actual power dissipated P = I^2 * R.

questions.text: An electric refrigerator rated 400 W operates 8 hours/day. What is the cost of energy to operate it for 30 days at ₹ 3.00 per kWh?
questions.explanation: Total energy consumed in 30 days = 400 W * 8 h/day * 30 days = 96,000 Wh = 96 kWh. Cost = 96 kWh * ₹ 3.00/kWh = ₹ 288.00.
hints: Calculate total energy in watt-hours (Power × hours × days).
Convert watt-hours to kilowatt-hours by dividing by 1000.
